title: Fault Merge collapses separate sticks and interleaves their ordered nodes
problem: Stick identity in the renderer is the section string, derived from a section label plus native stick_id. Merge concatenates incoming picks without giving their sticks a collision-free identity. Reused stick IDs/section labels from another file or another import therefore group together; sorting by seq interleaves them. Merge also replaces, rather than accumulates, the fault provenance.
impact: This violates Fault → Stick → ordered picks and can persist a geometrically different fault. Retained old nodes can lose their original source attribution.
reproduction: Import one three-node stick with z=[100,101,102], then Merge a different source whose stick has the same native ID and section with z=[200,201,202]. After actual database close/reopen, one stick remains, ordered [100,200,101,201,102,202]; provenance lists only source1.FLT.
recommended_correction: Use a stable source/import-scoped stick key separate from its display label. Under Merge preserve independent stick groups, define intentional duplicate/reimport behavior, and retain provenance for all contributing sources.
regression_test: Merge two non-identical same-ID sticks and reimport the same file; compare ordered groups and source identities before/after close/reopen for New/Merge/Replace.
existing_test_gap: test_kingdom_native.py checks single-import topology and reopen; its app-flow existing-name test exercises New name, not colliding Merge. Those tests cannot establish this invariant.
classification: Confirmed current-code behavior; reproduced with controlled fixtures

title: IHS 297 writes feet-valued tops into metre wells while converting the survey
function: header_values / tops / ip_test / fm_test / cores / apply / _children
problem: The source length convention is feet. store_survey is given length_unit="ft" and converts correctly, but tops, test intervals and core intervals are written as raw numbers. Existing-well fill keeps the well's metre unit. Header depth/elevation handling can also mix source and target conventions.
impact: Related records within one well no longer share a physical depth system. This can misplace tops/zones/tests relative to the trajectory and logs. In overwrite mode, assigning elevation_units="ft" is also not a conversion of existing metre data.
reproduction: On an existing metre well, import a 1,000-ft top and a vertical survey ending at 1,000 ft. The survey is stored at 304.8 m; the top is stored at 1,000 m.
recommended_correction: Convert every incoming length field to the established target well unit before writing, including elevations, TD, tops, cores and tests, or reject a unit mismatch explicitly. Do not change the well unit without a complete, explicit data conversion.
regression_test: Feet and metre existing wells in fill/overwrite modes; compare all related MD/TVD/elevation/recovery fields to hand conversions after reopen. Include wells with existing interpreted metre data.
existing_test_gap: test_native_ihs297.py validates feet-based fixture wells and survey handling but has no metre-target integration case. Its counts/idempotence checks would still pass.
classification: Confirmed current-code behavior; reproduced with controlled fixtures

title: A header-only 297 fill import deletes earlier tops, tests and cores
problem: For every included existing well, _children unconditionally deletes IHS 297 tops, tests and cores before writing incoming children. The deletion is source-wide, independent of the selected file and whether that record family appears in it. The comment says this file's earlier import is replaced, but the predicate is broader.
impact: A partial delivery can erase prior project records during a fill import, with no child-deletion preview. Prior tests have source_file provenance, but deletion does not use it; tops and cores have only broad vendor markers.
reproduction: Import a well with an IHS top. Import a second parsed file containing the same well header and no tops using default fill policy. The existing top count goes from one to zero. The same unconditional deletion applies to IHS tests and marked cores.
recommended_correction: Preserve absent record families in fill/partial-update workflows. Scope replacement to explicit source/file or stable record identities, and require an explicit complete-snapshot replacement policy with a deletion preview when absence means deletion.
regression_test: A header-only and a tests-only second delivery must preserve unrelated prior children; explicitly authorized full replacement should delete only the intended records and roll back on failure.
existing_test_gap: test_reimport_is_idempotent_and_no_duplicate_wells compares counts for the same complete file. It does not test partial deliveries or different file provenance; the existing fill test preserves only another interpreter's tops.
classification: Confirmed current-code behavior; reproduced with controlled fixtures

title: Replace with an out-of-survey horizon origin clears and saves the existing horizon
problem: The selected origin is parsed but a resulting empty placement is still submitted under Replace. apply_horizons clears the old grid before assigning zero incoming picks. The app then saves and reports a successful zero-pick import.
impact: A wrong origin or incompatible survey can erase a valid interpreted surface instead of rejecting an import that cannot place anything. Preview placement uses the offered origin before the user's final edited origin.
reproduction: Through the actual app import method with its preview callback: first import H02503 at 6448/3460 (1,830 picks), then choose 0/0 and Replace on the same survey. The horizon becomes empty, save is called, and the status says 10300 (0 picks).
recommended_correction: Recompute and validate placement after the final origin choice and before mutation. Reject zero-usable-pick replacement and preserve the old horizon; an intentional clear must be a separate explicit action. Report partial coverage before destructive replacement.
regression_test: Wrong origin, all picks outside and a valid partial overlap under every policy; assert old grids and persisted data survive rejected imports.
existing_test_gap: Current native app tests cover missing units, different sizes, New name and Cancel. They do not combine an edited invalid origin with Replace.
classification: Confirmed current-code behavior; reproduced with controlled fixtures

title: The approved 29-symbol catalog makes the build self-test fail
problem: Geo's self_test asserts len(SYMBOLS)>=100 although the shipped active catalog has exactly the required 29 symbols. The Windows build invokes that self-test and aborts on its nonzero exit.
impact: The release build gate rejects a valid shipped catalog. This is a concrete stale assertion, not evidence that the WSD is missing or that Windows itself was executed here.
reproduction: Run app.py --self-test with the unmodified archive and a fresh user settings path. It exits 1; the application log records AssertionError: well symbol catalogue (.WSD) missing at the >=100 assertion.
recommended_correction: Validate the required shipped resource/catalog contract rather than the obsolete size threshold; distinguish resource presence from user-added/deactivated entries. Retain the failure gate.
regression_test: Execute the real source self-test and frozen Windows self-test with the 29 shipped codes, fresh settings and valid edited catalogs.
existing_test_gap: test_exactly_the_29_approved_symbols passes, while PDF packaging tests mostly inspect build configuration. No default suite test executes this real Geo self-test end-to-end.
classification: Confirmed current-code behavior; reproduced with controlled fixtures

title: Rejected duplicate-code edits still change and persist status mappings
problem: apply_form rewrites mappings and shared-geometry references before validation. On rejection it restores only the edited entry. For GAS→OIL, the duplicate rename is rejected, but IHS GAS mappings now point to OIL and the restored catalog validates successfully.
impact: A user can save a change that the editor explicitly refused. Subsequent IHS imports can assign oil symbols to gas wells; a malformed-name attempt can instead leave the working catalog unsavable.
reproduction: Load GAS, change Code to OIL, click Apply and receive the duplicate-code error. GAS is restored, but the IHS GAS mapping is OIL. Save, reload the catalog: the wrong mapping persists.
recommended_correction: Validate a complete candidate copy before publishing any changes, or roll back every dependent mapping/geometry reference together with the entry. Rejection must leave the entire working catalog unchanged.
regression_test: Snapshot all entries/mappings/render references before failed duplicate/invalid/cyclic renames and assert complete equality afterward, then Save/restart and resolve representative statuses.
existing_test_gap: test_duplicate_code_and_invalid_alias_are_refused asserts only that the GAS entry is restored, not that dependent mappings remain unchanged.
classification: Confirmed current-code behavior; reproduced with controlled fixtures

title: Valid JSON with malformed catalog fields can prevent Geo and Seismic startup
problem: load catches file/JSON parsing errors, then assumes symbols is a mapping and directly converts symbol_id/scale/show counts. A structurally valid JSON file with scale="oops" or symbols as a list raises uncaught ValueError/AttributeError. Invalid render definitions can also be installed without validate().
impact: A bad local settings file becomes an application startup dependency. There is no safe fallback/diagnostic at the field-validation boundary for these cases.
reproduction: Load {"symbols":{"OIL":{"scale":"oops"}}}: ValueError. Load {"symbols":["x"]}: AttributeError. These reach current(), called during Geo and Seismic initialization. An unknown body loads/installs even though validate subsequently identifies it.
recommended_correction: Validate schema/types and the complete catalog before installation. Preserve the malformed file for diagnosis, surface a useful settings error and use a known-safe catalog rather than crashing or installing invalid geometry.
regression_test: Malformed but parseable JSON for every field/container, unknown geometry, bad mappings, NaN/Inf scales and future versions; open Geo/Seismic with fresh and malformed settings in source/frozen layouts.
existing_test_gap: Catalog tests cover valid persistence/import and editor validation. They do not exercise malformed on-disk user settings through startup.
classification: Confirmed current-code behavior; reproduced with controlled fixtures

title: Each newly created 297/298 well triggers another full well-table scan
function: refresh_api14 / api_owners / add_well / native import apply loops
problem: Each add_well duplicate check calls refresh_api14, whose UPDATE predicate compares api14_src with api_uwi across the table. EXPLAIN reports SCAN wells even when every normalized API is already current.
impact: A batch creating M wells in an N-well project performs roughly N×M normalization checks in addition to inserts. IHS 298's creation loop also precedes its monthly-row progress/cancellation callbacks, so a large new-well phase can remain unresponsive.
reproduction: Creating 100 wells through IHS 298 produced 100 full-table refreshes and one commit. Apply took 0.0225 s on an empty project and 0.8063 s with 112,000 seeded wells. Planning took 0.0084/0.1151 s. These are controlled observations, not a full-file throughput guarantee.
recommended_correction: Refresh/validate normalization once at a safe bulk boundary and maintain known-clean inserted/updated rows, while keeping indexed exact-API duplicate checks. Add progress/cancellation during well creation. Do not remove identity protection.
regression_test: Trace a bulk import and bound full-table refresh count independently of imported well count; include prior raw SQL API edits, duplicate protection, 100k-well projects and cancellation during creation.
existing_test_gap: Existing tests establish an index on exact API lookup and import correctness, but do not catch the separate full-table refresh before every indexed lookup.
classification: Confirmed current-code behavior; reproduced with controlled fixtures

title: Native Kingdom imports overwrite a persistence-failure warning with success
problem: save_now catches sqlite3.Error and writes Interpretation not saved yet, without returning a failure outcome. Native import methods immediately replace that status with Kingdom ... imported and return success.
impact: An import can be present only in memory while the user is told it succeeded. The old database transaction may remain safe, but durability failure is hidden and closing can lose work.
reproduction: Inject sqlite3.OperationalError("synthetic disk full") at save_interpretation while using the actual app save_now/import methods. Status first reports the error, then says Kingdom horizons imported: 10300 (1,830 picks); an ordinary success result is returned.
recommended_correction: Return/propagate a durable-save outcome and preserve a prominent unsaved/error state. Only report a saved import after successful persistence; define retry/rollback behavior without discarding the working interpretation.
regression_test: Inject save failures for horizons and faults through the app path, assert old durable data survives, the error remains visible, no false durable success is returned, and a successful retry clears the unsaved state.
existing_test_gap: Native app-flow tests replace save_now with a counter. Store round-trip tests validate successful writes; neither catches this app/store failure interaction.
evidence: save-failure-evidence.json; injected I/O/database failure, not observed client disk failure
classification: Confirmed current-code behavior; reproduced with controlled fixtures

title: Corrupt native files can escape the promised import diagnostic path
problem: Directory entries are unpacked without checking available bytes. read_fault wraps CFBError only from opening the container, not later stream reads. read_native catches KingdomNativeError only.
impact: A truncated horizon or damaged FLT stream can raise struct.error/CFBError directly instead of producing an unreadable-file diagnostic. In a mixed selection it interrupts preview of otherwise valid files. No database corruption was established by this probe.
reproduction: Truncate H02503 at 1,750, 2,400 or 4,200 bytes: unpack_from raises outside read_native handling. Mutate an FLT Fault_Data directory start to an invalid sector: CFBError escapes while reading the stream.
recommended_correction: Check every declared count/range before decoding and normalize expected malformed-container/stream exceptions into the native importer error/diagnostic type. Include path and offending region; do not broadly suppress programming errors.
regression_test: Truncate around every directory/sector/tile boundary, corrupt stream references/counts, and import a mix of valid/bad files. Assert useful diagnostics and unchanged project data.
existing_test_gap: Current not-a-file tests reject invalid signatures; a few invalid outer headers do not cover inner truncation/stream failures.
classification: Confirmed current-code behavior; reproduced with controlled fixtures

title: Native horizon origin placement silently assumes unit line/trace increments
problem: with_origin numbers native grid indices by adding origin+index. No increment is used or checked. Equal grid shape enables an origin default even when selected survey line/trace numbers increment by 2 or are otherwise non-unit.
impact: On such a selected survey, some samples are dropped and others map to different bins. The supported unit-increment layout should be enforced explicitly rather than implied by matching dimensions.
reproduction: A three-node diagonal on a 3×3 grid, selected survey lines [100,102,104] and traces [200,202,204], becomes numbered [100,101,102]. Only two samples place, at bins (0,0) and (1,1), so native grid index (2,2) moves to bin (1,1).
recommended_correction: Either reject unsupported survey numbering increments with a clear diagnostic or explicitly map native grid indices using a validated survey origin and numbering interval. Do not infer compatibility from shape alone.
regression_test: Unit, doubled, descending and irregular selected survey numbering; assert correct placement or a pre-mutation rejection. Add both app preview and engine tests.
existing_test_gap: The native fixtures and geometry helper use unit increments, so current orientation tests do not exercise this accepted-input assumption.
evidence: native-edge-evidence.json: increment_two_survey; synthetic survey-numbering boundary, not a claim about the supplied Kingdom project
classification: Confirmed current-code behavior; reproduced with controlled fixtures

title: Duplicate SYM numbers save successfully and make numeric resolution order-dependent
problem: Validation checks duplicate codes but not SYM-number ambiguity. Duplicate copies the same SYM number. find_symbol(number) returns the first matching catalog entry, even if it represents a different status/geometry.
impact: Numeric symbol inputs can silently resolve to a different code after editing or reordering the catalog. Distinct code-based resolution remains unambiguous.
reproduction: Assign OIL the GAS SYM number 2; validate returns no problems and save succeeds. find_symbol("2") then returns OIL rather than GAS.
recommended_correction: Define an explicit SYM alias policy: reject/warn on conflicting active numeric identities or require a code when a numeric lookup is ambiguous. Preserve deliberate equivalent aliases only with clear semantics.
regression_test: Duplicate distinct-geometry SYM values, reorder/restart, WSD import/export and numeric importer resolution; never silently choose the first conflicting meaning.
existing_test_gap: Editor tests reject duplicate codes, and WSD tests round-trip valid builtins. Neither tests conflicting SYM values or duplicate's numeric identity.
classification: Confirmed current-code behavior; reproduced with controlled fixtures

title: Existing Map artists retain an old catalog style after catalog installation
function: install / marker_paths / _draw_well_symbols / refresh_wells / symbol-editor saved callback
problem: Catalog installation clears the marker-path function cache, but it does not invalidate existing Map symbol artists/draw keys. The editor's saved callback refreshes Well Manager rows, not open Map symbol layers.
impact: A saved style can appear updated in one view while an open Map keeps the old glyph/color. This is display inconsistency; the stored well code is unchanged.
reproduction: Draw an OIL well, install a catalog changing its color from #008000 to #123456, then process events and refresh_wells. The artist remains #008000. Calling set_wells to rebuild makes it #123456.
recommended_correction: Publish a catalog revision/install event to live views and include it in symbol-layer invalidation. Rebuild only affected symbol artists, without reloading geological data.
regression_test: Keep Map, Well Manager and relevant sections open while saving catalog color/geometry/scale edits; verify artist changes and stable data-read counts, including a large-map culling cache.
existing_test_gap: Current tests check cleared marker definitions and rendering in fresh figures, rather than an already painted live Map after editor save.
classification: Confirmed current-code behavior; reproduced with controlled fixtures

title: A picked native HZN cell with a non-finite value is counted and imported without validation
problem: The mask codes correctly govern picked/unpicked status, but accepted codes are not combined with a finite-value check. A corrupted NaN/Inf pick reaches placement and assignment and counts as an imported pick.
impact: A non-finite source value can clear an existing finite cell during Merge or Replace while the success count still includes it. This is separate from the three genuinely unpicked H02503 cells, which are handled correctly.
reproduction: Change one picked H02503 float to NaN while retaining its picked mask code. Native read returns 1,830 picks including one non-finite z, with no malformed-value diagnostic.
recommended_correction: Validate finite numeric pick values separately from authoritative validity flags. Reject/report malformed picked cells and define safe replacement semantics; never repair the three unpicked cells from CSV truth.
regression_test: NaN/Inf under picked flags, stale finite values under unpicked flags, and Merge onto an existing finite cell. Assert diagnostics/counts and safe old-cell behavior.
existing_test_gap: The current H02503 regression correctly verifies the three mask exclusions and ordinary values but does not test malformed numbers under valid picked codes.
classification: Confirmed current-code behavior; reproduced with controlled fixtures

title: Save closes the Symbol Editor without warning about unapplied form edits
problem: Fields update the live preview, but Save serializes only the working catalog and does not apply/check dirty form fields. The separate Apply to the symbol button is required.
impact: Users can see a changed preview, click Save and lose that form edit without warning. The explicit Apply button makes this a contained usability issue rather than catalog corruption.
reproduction: Change GAS description in the form to Edited in form and click Save without Apply. save returns true and closes; reloaded description is still Gas Well.
recommended_correction: Apply/validate a dirty current form on Save, or explicitly warn that the form has unapplied changes and keep the dialog open. Preserve Cancel semantics.
regression_test: Edit→Save, edit→Apply→Save, invalid edit→Save, changing selection with dirty fields and Cancel; make retained/dropped edits explicit.
existing_test_gap: Current editor persistence tests call apply_form before save, so they do not exercise the common direct-Save path.
classification: Confirmed current-code behavior; reproduced with controlled fixtures
